messages:
alexa: Heads up — we've been getting client reports of streams that close halfway through a JSON object. Console shows a spike in "incomplete_frame" from eu-west around 01:14 UTC.
tom: I see it too. Server logs show a read error 'connection reset by peer' then immediate incomplete_frame and close. Mostly small frames (300-600B).
jules: Any infra churn? LB agent rolled at 01:10 per deploy-bot. Could be a proxy flush or aggressive FIN.
alexa: Sample log:
[01:14:12.007] ws:accept conn=conn42
[01:14:12.011] ws:read err=read: connection reset by peer
[01:14:12.011] stream:incomplete_frame conn=conn42 bytes=420
[01:14:12.011] ws:close reason=partial_frame

tom: Hypothesis: reverse proxy sends FIN during fragmented write. Our ws handler treats zero-length read as terminal. Minor tweak: do a single non-blocking retry (30ms) before closing. Opened hotfix branch ws-finish-retry.
jules: Add labels to metric stream_incomplete_frame_total: edge_agent_version, proxy_buffer_kb, client_ua. Also instrument trace spans for 24h with reconcile_id to see if agent rollbacks correlate.
alexa: Let's canary to eu-edge-canary and watch duplicate-frame counts. If retry causes duplicates we'll rollback.
deploy-bot: canary deploy: ws-finish-retry -> eu-edge-canary (2026.03.21-canary12)
tom: I'll own the rollback and watch the metric. If rate doesn't drop by 60% in 20m we rollback. Also add a Grafana card filtered by edge_agent_version.
jules: Follow-ups: add integration test that injects FIN mid-frame, add metric labels, add trace tags.
alexa: Thanks, we'll sync in 30m in #eng-platform.
